newsitem.title: USA: Aerial Communications sees March PCS launch.
newsitem.headline: Aerial Communications sees March PCS launch.

text.p: Aerial Communications Inc said Friday it is continuing to build its wireless phone network and expects to launch its personal communications services (PCS) in late March 1997.
The company said it expects total construction expenditures for 1997 of about $345 million.
The company said as of December 31, it had cleared 150 microwave paths and had commitments to clear 39 more, and enough have been cleared to allow the service to be launched in March.

"Costs incurred to date to clear microwave paths have been at or below projected levels and will have a favorable impact on capital expenditures in 1997," Aerial said in a statement. "The company expects construction expenditures for 1997 to total approximately $345 million."

The company said its PCS trials are underway in the Columbus, Ohio area. Aerial said it plans to launch the service with about 600 cell sites in place, which will provide wide-area metropolitan coverage in six areas.

The build-out phase, planned to be completed within 12 months of the service launch, is expected to include more than 1,000 total cell sites. After this phase, Aerial said its coverage is expected to be competitive with cellular operators.
